title: Locally bipartite subgraphs via multicolor Ramsey numbers
summary: A famous conjecture of Erdős and Hajnal (1969) states that for every integer $g\ge 4$ there is a smallest function $f_g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every graph of chromatic number at least $f_g(k)$ contains a subgraph of chromatic number $k$ and girth at least $g$. So far, this has only been proved for $g=4$ by Rödl (1977), with $f_4(k)$ bounded by a tower of height $Θ(k^2\log k)$. We exhibit a surprising connection between finding high-chromatic subgraphs of large odd-girth (avoiding short odd cycles) and lower-bounding multicolor Ramsey numbers of odd cycles.
